finding.claim: Exponential CPU traversal of the <use> reference graph (DoS). hasInfiniteLoop and countUse recurse over every path with no memo or visited set, and the nesting limit bounds depth only. A small SVG (about 15 layers of 5 elements, each referencing all 5 of the next layer) hangs or exhausts CPU in sanitize().
finding.source: Attacker-supplied SVG bytes passed to Sanitizer::sanitize() (src/Sanitizer.php:216).

trace.note: sanitize() constructs Resolver and calls collect()
processReferences links each subject to each <use> target
determineInvalidSubjects calls hasInfiniteLoop on every subject
each child is explored with no memo, so cost is the number of paths
isUseTagExceedingThreshold calls countUse on matching subjects
countUse recursion is also path-exponential; the threshold compares only after full computation

finding.guards_checked: Nesting limit (Subject.php:62) limits depth only. useThreshold (Sanitizer.php:681-698) is evaluated after the full countUse. No memoization or visited-set exists in either walk. Verified by reading; not executed.

finding.claim: Duplicate id values overwrite earlier subjects in the id map, so the threshold and loop checks see only the last element with that id. Browsers expand <use href> to the first element with that id, so an attacker can hide an expanding tree behind duplicate ids and bypass useThreshold.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied SVG containing duplicate id attributes.
finding.sink: Browser expansion of <use href="#id"> (first match in document order); the sanitizer keeps the <use> because it tracks the empty duplicate.

trace.note: collectIdentifiedElements queries //*[@id]
$this->subjects[$id] = new Subject(...) overwrites the earlier duplicate, so the last one wins
findByElementId returns only the tracked (last) copy
countUse on the empty last copy is 0, so the <use> is not removed

finding.guards_checked: useThreshold (Sanitizer.php:692-696) is the only control, and it sees the wrong element. Browser first-match behavior is an assumption from DOM getElementById semantics; not verified in a browser.

finding.claim: A <use> that is a descendant of the element it references causes Subject::addUse to throw LogicException, which escapes sanitize() uncaught. A single self-referencing element crashes the sanitizer for that input.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied SVG such as <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g id="a"><use href="#a"/></g></svg>.
finding.sink: Subject::addUse self-check throw (src/Subject.php:83-84); addUsedIn has the same throw (src/Subject.php:99-100).

trace.note: collect() is called with no try/catch
processReferences iterates use descendants of each subject
$subject->addUse($this->subjects[$useId]) with subject === target
throws LogicException 1570713416
sanitize() has no try/catch; exception propagates to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Resolver.php:140-149 try/catch covers only determineInvalidSubjects, not processReferences. The intended self-loop check (Resolver.php:141) is unreachable for the descendant case. Verified by reading; not executed.

finding.claim: Well-formed XML whose root element is not a single <svg> makes the XPath constructor throw LogicException instead of sanitize() returning false, breaking the documented string|false contract. The svg-scanner CLI aborts the batch on the same input.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied XML bytes that parse but have no <svg> root, for example <html/> or <foo/>.
finding.sink: XPath::handleDefaultNamespace throws when the root-svg count is not 1 (src/data/XPath.php:35-38).

trace.note: new XPath($this->xmlDocument) is constructed without a guard, after loadXML succeeded
constructor calls handleDefaultNamespace
getRootElements counts svg children of the document
throws LogicException 1570870568 when count != 1
resetAfter is skipped, so libxml_use_internal_errors(true) stays set
CLI calls sanitize() unguarded, so one bad file aborts the scan

finding.guards_checked: No try/catch around XPath construction in sanitize(). No early return for a non-svg root after loadXML. Verified by reading; not executed.

finding.claim: With removeRemoteReferences(true), remote references still survive: <image href="https://..."> (href is allowed by isHrefSafeValue and never checked by hasRemoteReference), unquoted fill="url(https://...)", and style declarations with url(https://...). The flag only matches a whole-attribute quoted url(...), so the remote fetch the flag is meant to block still happens on render.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied SVG attributes and style text.
finding.sink: Remote fetch by the viewer when the SVG is rendered (remote reference left in the output).

trace.note: CLI enables removeRemoteReferences(true)
removal check runs only inside cleanAttributesOnWhitelist when the flag is set
isHrefSafeValue allows https:// and http:// values, so the href is kept
hasRemoteReference regex requires a quoted url(...) wrapper; unquoted and style-embedded forms do not match
returns false for values without a matching remote-reference form

finding.guards_checked: Flag gate (Sanitizer.php:444). Remote-ref regex (Sanitizer.php:596-603). Attribute href values are never passed to hasRemoteReference. <style> text is not inspected. Verified by reading; the remote-ref feature is opt-in and off by default.
